messages:
samir: FYI I've got a perf regression after switching the default KV layout to interleaved for paging experiments. Short-context workloads (seq=64/128) are slower.

leah: ugh. numbers?

samir: microbench (fused_flash path):
```
# before (separate-kv): mean token latency = 3.2 ms
# after  (interleaved-kv): mean token latency = 3.6 ms  <-- ~12.5% worse
# throughput (seq=128,batch=8): 310 tok/s -> 273 tok/s
```
nvprof snapshot shows increased uncoalesced loads + L1/TEX miss up ~18%.

anya: is this only for fp16 or bf16 too?

samir: repro with fp16 and bf16: fp16 shows the regression, bf16 is noisier but also worse in several runs. float32 (debug) not measurable due to compute-bound dominance.

max: can you paste the perf command you used?

samir: perf command and env:
```
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python perf/bench.py --model llama-13b \
  --dtype=float16 --kv-layout=interleaved --seq-len=128 --batch-size=8 --mode=generate
```
also profiler: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/nsys_interleaved`

ci-bot: perf-run finished: job 2024-03-11_11:05 (link: https://ci.internal/perf/1856789012) :white_check_mark:

leah: my quick hypothesis: interleaved layout changed stride/alignment so the fused FlashAttention kernel's vector loads are no longer 128-byte aligned -> warp fragmentation -> higher L2 and more global loads. Could also expose a bug in the strided index math for page boundaries.

anya: any sign of TLB misses or page-split counters?

samir: yes nvprof shows ctx: pt_miss and TLB miss counters spiked when crossing 64KB page boundaries in the interleaved layout. Also saw more `ld.global.ca` and fewer `ld.shared` coalesced operations in the kernel.

max: Does the fused kernel assume contiguous per-head KV layout? The interleaved layout packs heads across pages which can produce non-unit strides for head dim accesses.

leah: correct — fused kernels expect head-major contiguous K/V per beam to use vector loads. If stride != 16 or misaligned to 128 bytes they fall back to scalar codepaths or produce unaligned memaccesses.

samir: quick patch idea: add alignment pad to interleaved allocation to 128 bytes and ensure head_stride % 16 == 0, then re-run. If that fixes perf we still need a kernel-selector guard.

anya: also try forcing `--kv-layout=interleaved-chunked` where we chunk per-page so strides stay small (e.g., chunk size = 64). Might keep paging benefits while preserving contiguous small strides for kernels.

samir: ran two experiments:
```
1) interleaved + 128B pad -> token latency: 3.25 ms (almost back to baseline)
2) interleaved-chunked (chunk=64) -> token latency: 3.28 ms
```
both reduce L2 / TLB anomalies in profiler traces.

max: great. So the underlying issue is alignment/stride semantics, not the paging idea itself.

leah: action items:
- (samir) add allocator path that returns 128-byte aligned KV buffer for interleaved layout and add unit microbench.
- (anya) update kernel selector heuristic: prefer fused_flash when (dtype==fp16) AND (head_stride_bytes % 128 == 0) AND (seq_len <= 1024?) — otherwise pick paged/fallback kernel.
- (max) add diagnostic counters exposed to Console: per-request chosen-kernel, head_stride_bytes, alignment_pad_bytes, page-splits.

anya: one more nuance: bf16 path currently performs a cast -> fp16 on some devices in the runtime; ensure the cast doesn't re-pack into an unaligned buffer. We saw a case where cast created a temporary with natural alignment 16B, not 128B.

samir: noted. I'll also add an assert in debug builds when we pick fused_flash: check (uintptr_t(buffer) % 128 == 0) and head_stride alignment. That will catch CI regressions.

leah: do we want a fast rollback plan for Dedicated clusters? If this selector misfires we could regress many customers.

max: rollback = set default KV layout to separate-kv for all prod pools via runtime flag and bump rollout to canary until selector is in. Also add perf Canary: seq lenses 32/64/128 synthetic traffic.

anya: I'll prototype selector diff and post a PR with tests that simulate misaligned buffers.

samir: I'll push the allocator change and run the end-to-end perf suite. If green I'll attach nsys flame and updated numbers to the PR.

leah: thanks. small ask: include a microbench that toggles batch sizes/batching heuristics because some batching heuristics amplify the regression (small batch + many short sequences hit the slow path more).

samir: good call — adding batch sweep (1,2,4,8,16) to the bench.

ci-bot: deploy plan checklist added to perf ticket: https://issues.internal/PROD-6421 :white_check_mark:

max: ok. keep updates here. If someone spots a regression on CI tag me. :+1:

samir: will follow up with PR link and nsys captures in ~2 hours.
